record.summary: Statement of the AI Action Summit in Paris that sets six priorities: accessible AI to reduce digital divides; AI that is open, inclusive, transparent, ethical, safe, secure and trustworthy; innovation without market concentration; AI that shapes work and labour markets positively; sustainable AI; and international cooperation on governance. It commends the Bletchley and Seoul summits' work on AI safety and notes the voluntary commitments made there, says the signatories will keep addressing AI risks to information integrity and continue work on AI transparency, and reaffirms the commitment to a UN Global Dialogue on AI governance and an Independent International Scientific Panel on AI.
record.notes: Published on 11 February 2025, the second day of the AI Action Summit, held in Paris on 10 and 11 February 2025. The signatory list names 63 countries, the African Union Commission and the EU; the United States and the United Kingdom are not on it. A footnote limits the statement to civil applications and use of AI. Founding members launched a Public Interest AI Platform and Incubator under it. The International AI Safety Report 2025 (INT-09) was published ahead of the summit.

verification.note: Stored and read in this run: the Élysée English text (official; the snapshot of 17 Oct 2026 differs from that of 11 Oct 2026 only in the site's news links) and the French text (Élysée, alt-official), which confirm the title, the French title, the posting date of 11 February 2025, the six priorities, the paragraphs on safety, transparency and information integrity, the civil-use footnote and the signatory list of 63 countries, the African Union Commission and the EU; and DSIT's press release of 29 January 2025 (GOV.UK), which says the International AI Safety Report 2025 was published ahead of the summit hosted by France. Version 1's topic 'accountability & liability' has no support in the text and was dropped; the summary was rewritten from the text.

judgment.status_reasoning: A summit statement of priorities, posted by the Élysée on 11 February 2025; nothing in the stored texts (the English and French pages, both re-stored on 17 Oct 2026 with the same statement) shows a revision, withdrawal or later edition. 'Published (non-binding, current)' stands; it creates no obligations: the signatories affirm priorities, recognise needs and note voluntary commitments.
judgment.scope_reasoning: An intergovernmental summit declaration with AI safety and trustworthiness content; in scope with no note, like the other summit declarations (INT-03, INT-04).

extra_urls.reason: DSIT press release of 29 Jan 2025 (GOV.UK; the secondary source of INT-09), stored in this run: the International AI Safety Report 2025 was published ahead of the AI Action Summit hosted by France; supports the note and the issuing body's 'hosted by' clause
